facts.text: Rimouski holds status as the Marine Technopole of Quebec and is the province's cluster for the blue economy.
facts.evidence: Rimouski has earned status as the Marine Technopole of Quebec... Rimouski is now the cluster for the province of Quebec in the blue economy.

facts.text: ISMER-UQAR, on the Université du Québec à Rimouski campus, is the foremost French-language academic marine sciences research institute in North America.
facts.evidence: ISMER-UQAR is the foremost French-language academic research institute of marine sciences in North America, and occupies an entire building on the UQAR Rimouski campus.

facts.text: ISMER researchers and students use a 50 m research vessel, the Coriolis II, and an aquaculture laboratory supplied with seawater.
facts.evidence: Researchers and students have access to high tech equipment, a 50 m long research vessel (Coriolis II), and an aquaculture laboratory kept supplied with seawater.

facts.text: Health services are Rimouski's leading employer, and Telus is the next largest employer with 1,400 workers.
facts.evidence: Health services and related businesses are major employers, with 8,000 workers in health services in the lower St. Lawrence region; many of those in Rimouski... Telus is the next largest employer with 1,400

overview: Rimouski counted 48,935 residents in the 2021 Census, up 0.6 percent from 2016, spread across 339.13 square kilometres that take in former villages such as Le Bic and Pointe-au-Père. Growth is slow, so most new customers come from winning share rather than from newcomers.

The city is the service centre for the Bas-Saint-Laurent, with health care, a university, marine research and a large Telus operation drawing people in from the surrounding region. Businesses here compete in French for a stable, loyal market where reputation and referrals carry real weight.

byService.lead-generation: With Rimouski's population growing only 0.6 percent since 2016, lead generation should focus on winning customers from competitors and on regional buyers who travel in for services.

byService.website-development: A Rimouski website should be built in French first, load quickly on mobile and make it easy for hospital, university and Telus staff to book or order after hours.
byService.branding: In a stable city of about 49,000 people, Rimouski branding works best when it feels rooted in the region, its maritime identity and long-term community relationships.
